Kolmogorov-Arnold Network-Based Denoising for LiDAR Odometry in High-Reflectivity Regions
(2026) IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.1109/TIM.2026.3670528
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105031927095?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Beijing University of Chemical Technology, College of Information Science and Technology, Beijing, 100029, China; New Jersey Institute of Technology, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Newark, 07102, NJ, United States
ABSTRACT: Reliable odometry is important for robots operating in environments with highly reflective surfaces. Yet its high reliability is difficult to achieve since intense reflection-induced noise gives rise to spurious points and feature mismatches. For purely LiDAR-based systems, this motion distortion further exacerbates due to the absence of auxiliary sensors. To solve these problems, this work proposes a denoising framework based on Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN) by integrating the strengths of multi-layer perceptrons and spline functions for robust point cloud denoising. The method can learn to model complex noise distributions and adaptively tunes its parameters to local noise intensity, ensuring the retention of critical geometric features. To enable real-time compensation for motion distortion and adaptive process noise adjustment according to motion confidence, this work proposes a multi-iteration optimization scheme that embeds denoising directly into the state estimation pipeline is designed. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks and real-world experiments validate the superiority of our method in achieving accurate and stable LiDAR localization in high-reflectivity scenarios over the state of the art. © 1963-2012 IEEE.

Liu Z., Kim J.I.

Autonomous Earthwork Machinery for Urban Construction: A Review of Integrated Control, Fleet Coordination, and Safety Assurance
(2025) Buildings, 15 (14), art. no. 2570, Cited 6 times.
DOI: 10.3390/buildings15142570
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105011635610?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Department of Architecture and Civil Engineering, City University of Hong Kong, 999077, Hong Kong; School of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Kookmin University, Seoul, 02707, South Korea
ABSTRACT: Autonomous earthwork machinery is gaining traction as a means to boost productivity and safety on space-constrained urban sites, yet the fast-growing literature has not been fully integrated. To clarify current knowledge, we systematically searched Scopus and screened 597 records, retaining 157 peer-reviewed papers (2015–March 2025) that address autonomy, integrated control, or risk mitigation for excavators, bulldozers, and loaders. Descriptive statistics, VOSviewer mapping, and qualitative synthesis show the output rising rapidly and peaking at 30 papers in 2024, led by China, Korea, and the USA. Four tightly linked themes dominate: perception-driven machine autonomy, IoT-enabled integrated control systems, multi-sensor safety strategies, and the first demonstrations of fleet-level collaboration (e.g., coordinated excavator clusters and unmanned aerial vehicle and unmanned ground vehicle (UAV–UGV) site preparation). Advances include centimeter-scale path tracking, real-time vision-light detection and ranging (LiDAR) fusion and geofenced safety envelopes, but formal validation protocols and robust inter-machine communication remain open challenges. The review distils five research priorities, including adaptive perception and artificial intelligence (AI), digital-twin integration with building information modeling (BIM), cooperative multi-robot planning, rigorous safety assurance, and human–automation partnership that must be addressed to transform isolated prototypes into connected, self-optimizing fleets capable of delivering safer, faster, and more sustainable urban construction. © 2025 by the authors.

A Multisensor Fusion Localization Method to Enhance Autonomous Navigation in Off-Road Environments
(2026) IEEE Internet of Things Journal, 13 (4), pp. 6017 - 6028, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.1109/JIOT.2025.3634116
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105022289346?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: College of Mechatronics and Control Engineering, Shenzhen University, Shenzhen, 518060, China; Shenzhen City Joint Laboratory of Autonomous Unmanned Systems and Intelligent Manipulation, Shenzhen, 518060, China; Guangdong Provincial Laboratory of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Economy (Shenzhen), Shenzhen, 518060, China
ABSTRACT: This article develops a real-time localization framework based on multisensor fusion for the autonomous navigation of mobile robots in challenging off-road environments. The proposed framework employs a hybrid coupling strategy at its front-end, which integrates inertial measurement unit (IMU) data with global navigation satellite system (GNSS) and LiDAR. As a consequence, GNSS inertial odometry (GIO) and LiDAR inertial odometry (LIO) are created, and these are crucial for achieving precise localization in real-time. The RGB-height-intensity descriptor is used to improve the precision of loop closure detection while maintaining search efficiency. This is achieved by integrating surface reflectance data from the LiDAR intensity channel and RGB data from camera images. Finally, in the back-end procedure of this framework, the accuracy of posture estimation is enhanced by the optimization of odometry and loop closure factors. In addition, a framework of real-time localization and autonomous navigation is developed and implemented on a wheeled robot to verify the proposed real-time localization framework. The experimental results indicate the framework exhibited higher performance in off-road environments, where conventional localization techniques generally degrade. © 2014 IEEE.
AUTHOR KEYWORDS: Autonomous navigation; ground robot; localization; multisensor fusion; off-road terrain

Three-dimensional recognition method of steelmaking area based on PointNet++
(2025) Proceedings of SPIE - The International Society for Optical Engineering, 13801, art. no. 138010E, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.1117/12.3077412
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105022515645?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: School of Mechanical Engineering, Anhui University of Technology, Ma’anshan, China
ABSTRACT: Aiming at the problems of poor adaptability, inaccurate feature extraction, and excessive reliance on light in traditional target recognition algorithms for handling robots, a multi-objective classification method has been proposed based on an integrated attention mechanism module of PointNet++ network. The Context Anchor Attention mechanism was incorporated into the feature extraction layer. Firstly, a multi-line LiDAR was used to collect point clouds and modify them according to Modelnet40 dataset format; 80% of the dataset was used to train the network, while the remaining 20% was used to test. The experimental results indicate that the overall classification accuracy of the proposed method in the steelmaking area dataset reaches 96.97%, surpassing the performance of the original PointNet++ classification network and meeting the operational requirements for the handling robot to identify targets accurately. © 2025 SPIE.

Design and application of a multi-source sensor data fusion system based on a robot phenotype platform
(2025) Fruit Research, 5, art. no. e032, Cited 3 times.
DOI: 10.48130/frures-0025-0023
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105014634952?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: National Engineering Research Center for Agro-Ecological Big Data Analysis and Application, Anhui University, Hefei, 230039, China; Information Technology Research Center, Beijing Academy of Agriculture and Forestry Sciences, Beijing, 100097, China; Beijing Key Lab of Digital Plant, National Engineering Research Center for Information Technology in Agriculture, Beijing, 100097, China
ABSTRACT: The compact, high-throughput phenotyping platform, characterized by its portability and small size, is well-suited for crop phenotyping across diverse environments. However, integrating multi-source sensors to achieve synchronized data acquisition and analysis poses significant challenges due to constraints in load capacity and available space. To address these issues, we developed a robotic platform specifically designed for phenotyping greenhouse strawberries. This system integrates an RGB-D camera, a multispectral camera, a thermal camera, and a LiDAR sensor, enabling the unified analysis of data from these sources. The platform accurately extracted key phenotypic parameters, including canopy width (R² = 0.9864, RMSE = 0.0185 m) and average temperature (R2 = 0.8056, RMSE = 0.1732 °C), with errors maintained below 5%. Furthermore, it effectively distinguished between different strawberry varieties, achieving an Adjusted Rand Index of 0.94, underscoring the value of detailed phenotyping in variety differentiation. Compared to conventional UGV-LiDAR systems, the proposed platform is more cost-effective, efficient, and scalable, with enhanced data consistency, making it a promising solution for agricultural applications. © The Author(s).

DOI: 10.1117/12.3071030
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105011028753?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Comarvel Intelligent Technology Company Limited, Yantai, China; Shibuzi Primary School, Anqiu, China
ABSTRACT: This paper conducts an in-depth investigation into the application of Laser SLAM and Visual SLAM technologies in the navigation system of intelligent shore power robots. By integrating the high-precision mapping capability of Laser SLAM with the rich environmental perception capacity of Visual SLAM, a composite navigation system design scheme is proposed. The system initially constructs port application scenario maps using both Laser SLAM and Visual SLAM technologies, generating point cloud maps and vector maps, followed by map annotation and verification. Through map matching, the system achieves precise robot positioning. Combined with obstacle detection information from multi-sensors (such as lidar, ultrasonic sensors, etc.), it accomplishes autonomous localization, path planning, and dynamic obstacle avoidance functions. © COPYRIGHT SPIE.

Sequential Probabilistic Descriptor via Uncertainty-Aware Multi-Modal Fusion for Safety-Critical Place Recognition
(2026) IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters, 11 (4), pp. 5214 - 5221, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.1109/LRA.2026.3669806
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105032495279?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: School of Automation, Southeast University, Changsha, 410017, China; Key Laboratory of Measurement and Control of CSE, Ministry of Education, Nanjing, 210096, China; SF Technology, Shenzhen, 518000, China
ABSTRACT: —The success of loop closure and global map consistency largely relies on robust place recognition, making it a safety-critical capability for mobile robots in autonomous navigation. However, most existing approaches prioritize recognition accuracy while overlooking uncertainty estimation, which may lead to overconfident false predictions and compromise navigation safety. To address this limitation, this letter proposes a sequential multimodal probabilistic descriptor for place representation, explicitly modeling uncertainty at both the modality and decision levels. Specifically, sequential image and LiDAR inputs leverage temporal information and are encoded as probabilistic embeddings, followed by an uncertainty-aware fusion. By adaptively balancing the contribution of each modality, prediction conflicts caused by sensor degradation are mitigated. Predictive uncertainty is further estimated through probabilistic combination rules, providing reliable confidence measures that allow downstream tasks to filter out high-uncertainty predictions. Extensive evaluations on NCLT, Oxford Robotcar and WildScenes datasets are conducted, covering long-term tasks, seasonal changes, illumination variations, and unstructured natural environments. Results show that the proposed method achieves superior performance across diverse conditions and provides well-calibrated uncertainty estimates that enable reliable failure detection, highlighting its potential for deployment in safety-critical scenes. © 2026 IEEE. All rights reserved,

Omni-Bot: An Autonomous Inspection Robot for Underground Parking Garages Using Multi-Modal SLAM and Reinforcement Learning-Based Navigation
(2025) 2025 International Ubiquitous Positioning, Indoor Navigation and Location-Based Services Conference, UPINLBS 2025, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.1109/UPINLBS68186.2025.11468399
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105038019563?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Hangzhou Institute for Advanced Study, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Hangzhou, China; College of Automation Engineering, Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Nanjing, China; Advanced Laser Technology Lab of Anhui Province, Anhui, China
ABSTRACT: Underground parking garages present a challenging sensing and navigation setting due to the absence of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) signals, limited illumination, and repetitive structural motifs. We develop Omni-Bot, an autonomous inspection platform that integrates a four-view panoramic industrial camera array, a 360° Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) sensor (Livox Mid-360), and a highfrequency inertial measurement unit (IMU) to realize multimodal odometry and mapping through the proposed Omni-LIVO pipeline. On top of this state estimator, a hybrid local planning framework merges a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based reinforcement learning (RL) policy with a Dynamic Window Approach (DWA) feasibility filter, ensuring that learned maneuvers remain dynamically safe. A lightweight image enhancement module stabilizes low-light observations before YOLO-based semantic detections are projected into the LiDAR grid map via calibrated camera-LiDAR extrinsics, which enables target tagging without perturbing the navigation controller. Field trials conducted in operational garages report sub- 0.20 m mapping error over kilometer-scale traversals, a 97 % navigation success rate with minimum 0.42 m obstacle clearance, and robust licenseplate recognition under severe illumination degradation. These results demonstrate that the proposed perception and planning stack delivers a practical inspection solution for GNSS-denied, visually and geometrically degraded indoor environments. © 2025 IEEE.

AUTHOR FULL NAMES: Lin, Kexuan (59736523100); Sun, Mingchu (60237222400); Wang, Xuefei (60236933500); Zhai, Qiukai (60237779900)

Design and Application of an Autonomous Mobile Grasping Robot System Based on Deep Learning
(2025) Advances in Transdisciplinary Engineering, 75, pp. 1413 - 1425, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.3233/ATDE250895
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105024678810?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: College of Automation, Xi 'An Jiaotong University, Shaanxi, Xi'an, 710049, China; College of Management, Xi 'An Jiaotong University, Shaanxi, Xi'an, 710049, China; College of Microelectronics, Xi 'An Jiaotong University, Shaanxi, Xi'an, 710049, China; College of Artificial Intelligence, Xi 'An Jiaotong University, Shaanxi, Xi'an, 710049, China
ABSTRACT: This paper presents the design and experimental validation of a comprehensive autonomous mobile robot (AMR) system for intelligent warehousing and material handling tasks. To address the challenges of environmental perception and precise operation in complex settings, the system integrates multi-sensor fusion technology, utilizing depth cameras, Inertial Measurement Unit (IMUs), Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR), and ultrasonic sensors to enhance situational awareness and real-time decision-making. Core functionalities include deep learning-based object recognition (implemented using a custom-trained YOLOv5 model for high accuracy), robotic arm grasping and manipulation (leveraging MoveIt! for motion planning), Simultaneous Localization and Mapping based autonomous navigation and obstacle avoidance, and automated material sorting. The hardware platform features a four-wheeled mobile chassis equipped with a six-axis robotic arm and the aforementioned sensor suite, controlled via an ARM-based embedded system running the Robot Operating System (ROS) framework. Extensive experiments conducted in a simulated warehouse environment (2m x 4m) demonstrate the system's effectiveness: achieving over 98% material recognition accuracy, 100% successful grasping in controlled tests, and efficient path navigation with minimal cumulative error (∼4.83 cm). Results confirm the system's high efficiency, accuracy, and reliability in integrated tasks encompassing perception, grasping, sorting, and autonomous mobility, providing significant technical support for the practical deployment of AMRs in logistics and industrial automation. © 2025 IOS Press.

GuardianEye: IoT-Assisted Multi-Functional Drone Architecture for Firefighting, Agricultural Monitoring, and Scientific Research
(2025) 2025 28th International Conference on Computer and Information Technology, ICCIT 2025, pp. 5602 - 5607, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.1109/ICCIT68739.2025.11491503
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105041626212?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: The University of Alabama, AL, United States; Khulna Uni. of Engineering & Technology, Khulna, Bangladesh; Ahsanullah Uni. of Sci. & Technology, Dhaka, Bangladesh; Port City International University, Chittagong, Bangladesh
ABSTRACT: The integration of IoT and unmanned aerial systems has enabled transformative solutions for emergency response, precision agriculture, and environmental monitoring. This paper presents GuardianEye, a quadcopter platform combining edge computing, autonomous navigation, and multi-sensor fusion (gas/thermal/ultrasonic) for adaptive field operations. The system features an embedded computer for real-time vision processing (OpenCV, ¡200ms latency) and a flight controller supporting six-channel redundant control. For emergency scenarios, GuardianEye deploys microencapsulated fire retardants with 95% suppression efficiency, robotic manipulators for object retrieval, and AI-guided hose systems synchronized with realtime hazard detection. In agriculture, its ML-optimized spray nozzles achieve 0.5cm targeting precision while reducing chemical usage by 40%, concurrently generating NDVI crop health maps. The architecture integrates a 4K vision module, edge-based risk assessment algorithms (92% classification accuracy), and modular payload support for LiDAR or hyperspectral sensors. Field tests demonstrate 32% faster emergency response times and 90% spray accuracy, with IoT telemetry enabling live decision-making across disaster management, agritech, and ecological research applications. Validated in diverse environments, GuardianEye bridges critical gaps between conventional practices and smart technologies, offering measurable improvements in operational safety (60% reduced responder exposure) and resource efficiency (35% less water usage in firefighting). This work details its bio-inspired mechanical design, ROS-based autonomy stack, and large-scale deployment results, establishing new benchmarks for intelligent aerial systems in professional domains. © 2025 IEEE.

Loosely Coupled PPP/Inertial/LiDAR Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) Based on Graph Optimization
(2025) Remote Sensing, 17 (5), art. no. 812, Cited 2 times.
DOI: 10.3390/rs17050812
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/86000648299?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: School of Land Science and Technology, China University of Geosciences, Beijing, 100083, China; School of Surveying and Mapping, Information Engineering University, Zhengzhou, 450001, China; Chinese Academy of Surveying and Mapping, Beijing, 100039, China
ABSTRACT: Navigation services and high-precision positioning play a significant role in emerging fields such as self-driving and mobile robots. The performance of precise point positioning (PPP) may be seriously affected by signal interference and struggles to achieve continuous and accurate positioning in complex environments. LiDAR/inertial navigation can use spatial structure information to realize pose estimation but cannot solve the problem of cumulative error. This study proposes a PPP/inertial/LiDAR combined localization algorithm based on factor graph optimization. Firstly, the algorithm performed the spatial alignment by adding the initial yaw factor. Then, the PPP factor and anchor factor were constructed using PPP information. Finally, the global localization is estimated accurately and robustly based on the factor graph. The vehicle experiment shows that the proposed algorithm in this study can achieve meter-level accuracy in complex environments and can greatly enhance the accuracy, continuity, and reliability of attitude estimation. © 2025 by the authors.

Path Planning for Autonomous Unmanned Ground Vehicles in Underground Mining
(2025) AIAA Aviation Forum and ASCEND, 2025, Cited 1 times.
DOI: 10.2514/6.2025-3354
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105017958830?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Department of Mechanical Engineering, New Mexico Tech, Socorro, 87801, NM, United States; Department of Mineral Engineering, New Mexico Tech, Socorro, 87801, NM, United States; Department of Mining Engineering, University of Kentucky, Lexington, 40508, KY, United States
ABSTRACT: Autonomous robotic navigation in underground mining environments poses significant challenges due to confined spaces, poor lighting, and the absence of GPS signals. This study presents the design and implementation of an autonomous navigation system for the Husky unmanned ground vehicle (UGV), utilizing LIDAR-based Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) within the Robot Operating System (ROS) framework. The system enables real-time mapping, obstacle avoidance, and both global and local path planning in GPS-denied environments. The performance of navigation system was validated through simulations in Gazebo and field tests in two physical environments: the Bunker Lab at New Mexico Tech and the Missouri S&T Experimental Mine. These tests confirmed the Husky’s ability to navigate complex terrain and generate accurate 2D occupancy maps without prior environmental knowledge. © 2025 by the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Inc. All rights reserved.

ABSTRACT: Objective Three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction is a foundational task in computer vision, enabling a wide range of applications including robotics, autonomous driving, cultural heritage preservation, and digital twins. Although significant advances have been made, image-based reconstruction methods continue to face several challenges. Traditional pipelines based on structure-from-motion (SfM) and multi-view stereo (MVS) can generate dense point clouds and meshes, but they are often computationally expensive, sensitive to occlusions, and prone to failures in low-texture regions. Recently, Gaussian splatting techniques have emerged as an efficient alternative. Among them, 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) achieves impressive rendering speed and compact representation, yet it frequently suffers from structural distortions in thin-walled or geometrically complex areas. Conversely, 2D Gaussian splatting (2DGS) better captures fine surface details but provides insufficient geometric constraints for globally consistent reconstruction. To address these limitations, we propose Multimodal-2DGS, a novel multimodal reconstruction framework that integrates LiDAR point clouds with visual imagery under the 2D Gaussian representation. Our work is motivated by three key objectives: (i) to improve structural accuracy in thin-walled and complex regions where 3DGS performs poorly; (ii) to accelerate convergence and reduce redundancy in the activation of Gaussian primitives; and (iii) to enable robust reconstruction in multimodal settings by combining spatial priors from LiDAR with photometric cues from images. Methods The proposed Multimodal-2DGS framework is built upon 2D Gaussian primitives as its core representation, with its technical contributions comprising three key components. Initially, raw LiDAR point clouds undergo preprocessing involving statistical outlier removal and multiscale downsampling. These data are then co-registered with sparse point clouds from SfM through a coarse-to-fine alignment pipeline that combines global transformation estimation with iterative closest point (ICP) refinement, ensuring precise multimodal registration. The resulting fused point cloud subsequently guides the initialization and optimization process of the Gaussian primitives. First, we design a frequency-aware uniform and preserving controllable sampling (FUPCS) strategy. This method partitions the point cloud into high-frequency and low-frequency regions based on local curvature and density distributions. It preserves sharp edges and geometric boundaries while applying uniform downsampling to redundant low-frequency areas. Such dual-objective sampling enhances reconstruction fidelity and reduces computational redundancy. Second, we introduce a contour-based initialization mechanism employing farthest point sampling (FPS). Rather than initializing Gaussian primitives randomly across the scene, FPS selects representative points along major contours and within sparse regions. This approach provides strong global structural guidance, particularly for thin-walled structures such as walls, tables, and laboratory equipment, thereby lowering the optimization burden in early training stages. Third, we propose a frequency-guided dynamic Gaussian scheduling strategy. A nonlinear suppression function is designed to regulate the activation of Gaussian primitives. High-frequency regions are prioritized for early activation to capture critical geometric details promptly, while low-frequency regions are incorporated gradually. This scheduling balances reconstruction precision with computational efficiency, mitigates over-parameterization, and accelerates overall convergence. Results and Discussions We evaluate our method on three indoor scenes of varying complexity: a rest room, a meeting room, and a laboratory containing diverse equipment. Comparative experiments are conducted against several baseline methods, including 3DGS, Reduced-3DGS, Mini-Splatting, efficient density control for 3DGS (EDC-3DGS), and vanilla 2DGS. Quantitatively, Multimodal-2DGS consistently outperforms all baselines across evaluation metrics. In regions with thin-walled surfaces-such as walls, desks, and experimental boxes in the meeting room-the proposed method achieves a peak signal to noise ratio (PSNR) improvement of up to 3.90 dB and a structural similarity (SSIM) gain of 0.056 over 3DGS (Table 1). These results confirm that 2D Gaussian primitives possess an inherent advantage in modeling thin surfaces, while the integration of LiDAR priors further enhances reconstruction robustness. Ablation studies demonstrate the contribution of each proposed module. The FUPCS strategy shows strong edge-preservation capability (Fig. 5), leading to sharper reconstructions along geometric boundaries. The FPS-based initialization reduces optimization overhead in sparse regions and accelerates convergence in early training stages (Table 4). Furthermore, the frequency-guided dynamic scheduling mechanism improves convergence stability, enabling high-fidelity reconstruction within 3000 iterations (~300 s) - significantly faster than baseline methods (Fig. 4). Visually, Multimodal-2DGS generates reconstructions with sharper edges, more accurate contours, and fewer rendering artifacts compared to 3DGS and other baselines (Fig. 3). In the rest room, floral edges and leaf textures are better preserved. In the meeting room, fine details on surfaces such as projectors and tablecloths closely match the ground truth. In the laboratory, complex devices with thin components are faithfully reproduced, whereas 3DGS tends to produce blurred or distorted geometry. Overall, these findings highlight that combining LiDAR spatial priors with image-driven optimization effectively mitigates limitations of purely image-based reconstruction. The frequency-aware design ensures a balance between fidelity and efficiency, while the dynamic Gaussian scheduling offers a principled way to progressively activate primitives, thereby avoiding overfitting and enhancing training stability. Conclusions In this work, we present Multimodal-2DGS, a multimodal 3D reconstruction framework that integrates LiDAR point clouds and images under the 2DGS paradigm. The framework incorporates three key technical contributions-FUPCS, FPS-based initialization, and frequency-guided Gaussian scheduling-to achieve a compact, accurate, and computationally efficient reconstruction. Experimental evaluation across multiple indoor scenes demonstrates consistent superiority over state-of-the-art baselines in both quantitative metrics and qualitative visual fidelity. The principal advantages of Multimodal-2DGS are threefold: (i) it significantly improves reconstruction accuracy on thin-walled and geometrically complex surfaces; (ii) it accelerates convergence while reducing model redundancy; and (iii) it enhances robustness in multimodal settings by leveraging complementary structural and photometric guidance. These results underscore the importance of multimodal priors for achieving high-fidelity yet lightweight 3D reconstruction. Looking ahead, we plan to extend the framework to large-scale outdoor environments and dynamic scene reconstruction. Future work will also focus on adapting the method for use with low-cost sensing setups, such as consumer RGB-D cameras, and optimizing its deployment on mobile and edge computing platforms. We believe Multimodal-2DGS establishes a promising foundation for next-generation applications in robotics, autonomous driving, and digital twin systems. © 2026 Chinese Laser Press. Evaluation and Validation of SLAM Technologies in Indoor Environments
(2026) IAENG International Journal of Applied Mathematics, 56 (1), pp. 209 - 220, Cited 0 times.

ABSTRACT: This paper presents a comprehensive investigation into the diverse implementations of indoor SLAM technology, with a particular emphasis on LiDAR SLAM and Visual SLAM. The study systematically evaluates their performance and practical applicability across varying indoor environments. A detailed comparative analysis is conducted across three prominent 2D LiDAR SLAM methodologies—Karto SLAM, Hector SLAM, and Cartographer—as well as V-SLAM frameworks, including dense mapping with the Real-Time Appearance-Based Mapping and sparse mapping with the ORB-SLAM2. The evaluation framework encompasses empirical experiments, assessing critical performance metrics such as mapping accuracy, CPU or GPU usage, and robustness in key technical aspects, including loop closure detection, map resolution fidelity, and edge feature handling under diverse operational scenarios. In conclusion, this study elucidates the respective advantages and limitations of each SLAM technique, providing actionable insights for their deployment in specific indoor applications. Beyond offering a theoretical foundation for SLAM technology selection and optimization, this research contributes to the broader discourse on SLAM solutions, paving the way for future advancements in multi-scenario indoor localization and mapping systems. Future research endeavors will delve into the synergistic integration of diverse Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) technologies. More critically, the research will focus on systematically overcoming the inherent limitations of existing SLAM technologies, including computational bottlenecks, poor performance in dynamic or low-texture environments, and memory-intensive operations. © (2026), (International Association of Engineers). Simultaneous Localization and Mapping and Path Planning Algorithms Based on Radar-Visual Sensor Fusion in Unknown Environments [未知环境下基于雷视融合的同步定位构图与路径规划算法]

AFFILIATIONS: School of Automobile, Chang'an University, Xi'an, 710018, China
ABSTRACT: Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) and path planning are critical technologies in mobile robotics. However, existing research typically considers these processes separately, often requiring robots in unknown environments to perform mapping prior to path planning, thereby reducing navigation efficiency. To address this, the paper proposes a lidar-visual-inertial SLAM and local target A-star (LVISLAM_LTA*) algorithm that integrates mapping, localization, and path planning to enhance navigation performance in unfamiliar settings. This approach incorporates an intelligent perception with fusion-driven adaptive network (IP_FusionNet) algorithm for large-scale stereo vision data acquisition. Additionally, a feasible region detection module is introduced to provide navigable area information and improve computational efficiency for subsequent path planning. The feasible regions are represented through point cloud stitching and rasterization, forming a navigable area grid map. Furthermore, a local sub-goal-based path planning algorithm is developed to enable rapid online route computation. Experimental results on the KITTI dataset and a self-collected dataset demonstrate that this integrated approach achieves higher localization accuracy, reducing error by 24%, and constructs dense semantic maps that comprehensively and clearly depict the three-dimensional structure of the robot's environment. The proposed method also exhibits a 72.9% reduction in computation time compared to traditional algorithms, highlighting its efficiency and robustness in autonomous navigation tasks. © (2026), (Journal of Computer Engineering and Applications Beijing Co., Ltd.; Science Press). Terrain-Adaptive LiDAR-IMU SLAM with Multi-Feature fusion for complex underground environments

AFFILIATIONS: College of Geomatics, Xi’an University of Science and Technology, Xi’an, 710054, China; School of Geodesy and Geomatics, Wuhan University, Wuhan, 430079, China
ABSTRACT: Mobile robots empowered by Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) technology are becoming a key enabler of next-generation underground intelligence, providing essential support for intelligent management and safety monitoring of underground infrastructure. However, existing LiDAR SLAM methods overly rely on geometric features while neglecting point cloud intensity information and ground structural constraints, leading to reduced front-end robustness and limited back-end fusion performance. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a terrain-adaptive LiDAR-IMU SLAM framework that systematically integrates intensity-feature enhancement with Riemannian-manifold-based ground constraints. First, an adaptive feature-entropy enhancement method based on a spherical-coordinate intensity field is designed. A spherical intensity model with a six-grid averaging scheme is employed to extract reflection characteristics, significantly improving geometric matching accuracy and pose estimation robustness in low-texture underground environments. Second, a terrain-adaptation mechanism on Riemannian manifolds is designed, where a slope-dynamics model with normal-vector geodesic distances captures topographic variations. An exponential forgetting-weighted strategy within a sliding window further enables smooth adaptation to gradual-to-abrupt slope changes. Finally, a multi-feature fusion optimization module is developed, which dynamically balances geometric and intensity features within a sliding-window factor graph. This module jointly refines loop closure, LiDAR keyframe, and IMU pre-integration constraints. Extensive experiments conducted in representative underground environments, including subway tunnels, coal mine roadways, and underground parking lots facilities, demonstrate that the proposed method reduces vertical drift error by 67.78% and achieves a minimum absolute pose error of 0.254 m. These results confirm significant improvements in accuracy and robustness, providing a reliable technical foundation for intelligent underground inspection and infrastructure monitoring. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V. on behalf of International Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing, Inc. (ISPRS).

SMapper: A Multi-Modal Data Acquisition Platform for SLAM Benchmarking
(2026) Journal of Intelligent and Robotic Systems: Theory and Applications, 112 (1), art. no. 20, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.1007/s10846-026-02351-7
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105029768722?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Automation and Robotics Research Group (ARG), Interdisciplinary Centre for Security, Reliability, and Trust (SnT), University of Luxembourg, Luxembourg, L-1359, Luxembourg; Institute for Advanced Studies (IAS), University of Luxembourg, Esch-sur-Alzette, L-4365, Luxembourg; Faculty of Science, Technology and Medicine, University of Luxembourg, Esch-sur-Alzette, L-4365, Luxembourg
ABSTRACT: Advancing research in fields such as Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) and autonomous navigation critically depends on the availability of reliable and reproducible multimodal datasets. While several influential datasets have driven progress in these domains, they often suffer from limitations in sensing modalities, environmental diversity, and the reproducibility of the underlying hardware setups. To address these challenges, this paper introduces SMapper, a novel open-hardware, multi-sensor platform designed explicitly for, though not limited to, SLAM research. The device integrates synchronized LiDAR, multi-camera, and inertial sensing, supported by a robust calibration and synchronization pipeline that ensures precise spatio-temporal alignment across modalities. Its open and replicable design allows researchers to extend its capabilities and reproduce experiments across both handheld and robot-mounted scenarios. To demonstrate its practicality, we additionally release SMapper-light, a publicly available SLAM dataset containing representative indoor and outdoor sequences. The dataset includes tightly synchronized multimodal data and ground truth trajectories derived from offline LiDAR-based SLAM with sub-centimeter accuracy, alongside dense 3D reconstructions. Furthermore, the paper contains benchmarking results on state-of-the-art LiDAR and visual SLAM frameworks using the SMapper-light dataset. By combining open-hardware design, reproducible data collection, and comprehensive benchmarking, SMapper establishes a robust foundation for advancing SLAM algorithm development, evaluation, and reproducibility. The project’s documentation, including source code, CAD models, and dataset links, is publicly available at https://snt-arg.github.io/smapper_docs/. © The Author(s) 2026.

Longyun Z., Hongjun S., Jiupeng C., Zhen P.
AUTHOR FULL NAMES: Longyun, Zhao (58993893100); Hongjun, San (15521275800); Jiupeng, Chen (58994773200); Zhen, Peng (57216162339)

Laser Location of Mobile Robot Based on ICP Algorithm [基于 ICP 算法的移动机器人激光定位研究]
(2024) Laser and Optoelectronics Progress, 61 (8), art. no. 0811001, Cited 3 times.
DOI: 10.3788/LOP231307
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/85190837784?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Faculty of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering, Kunming University of Science and Technology, Yunnan, Kunming, 650500, China; Key Laboratory of Intelligent Manufacturing Technology for Advanced Equipment in Yunnan Province, Yunnan, Kunming, 650500, China
ABSTRACT: This study presents a localization method based on the improved iterative closest point (ICP) algorithm to solve the localization problems of mobile robots, such as low positioning accuracy and poor real-time positioning, in traditional 2D environments. The algorithm begins by establishing a pose search space, which systematically explored layer-by-layer, transitioning from lower to higher resolutions. To accelerate the search process and eliminate nonoptimal poses, partial point cloud scanning matching was executed synergistically with multipoint cloud density. Adoption of the frame-to-image method by the point cloud matching enabled the effective utilization of historical frame information. Further enhancements in positioning accuracy were achieved through the sparse matrix pose optimization for obtained optimal pose. Tests conducted on the SLAM Benchmark dataset show that the proposed algorithm is considerably more efficient, boasting a 1. 8‒4. 9 times efficiency gain over the popular Cartographer algorithm, and has less translation error. Real-world tests conducted on Turtlebot2 reveal that the proposed method exhibits substantially fewer positioning errors than Cartographer and Gmapping, showing superior realtime performance. Compared with the traditional adaptive Monte Carlo relocation (AMCL), the proposed method reduces mean translation errors by 0. 035 m and mean rotation errors by 0. 001 rad, resulting in higher relocation accuracy. © 2024 Universitat zu Koln. All rights reserved.

Li S., Chen S., Li X., Zhou Y., Wang S.
AUTHOR FULL NAMES: Li, Shengyu (57221943864); Chen, Shuolong (57841254900); Li, Xingxing (36617696300); Zhou, Yuxuan (57423744300); Wang, Shiwen (58426981900)
57221943864; 57841254900; 36617696300; 57423744300; 58426981900
Accurate and automatic spatiotemporal calibration for multi-modal sensor system based on continuous-time optimization
(2025) Information Fusion, 120, art. no. 103071, Cited 8 times.
DOI: 10.1016/j.inffus.2025.103071
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105000449408?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: School of Geodesy and Geomatics, Wuhan University, 129 Luoyu Road, Hubei, Wuhan, 430079, China
ABSTRACT: Current intelligent robotic applications, such as unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) and autonomous driving, generally rely on multi-modal sensor fusion to continuously strive towards higher levels of autonomy. To achieve this goal, accurate and consistent inter-sensor spatiotemporal relationship is a fundamental prerequisite for fusing heterogeneous sensor information. Nevertheless, current calibration frameworks typically necessitate specialized tools or additional infrastructures, rendering them labor-intensive and only applicable to certain sensor combinations. To address this issue, we propose an accurate and easy-to-use spatiotemporal calibration framework tailored to current primary sensors, including inertial measurement unit (IMU), LiDAR, camera and Radar. This calibration framework can be seamlessly extended to other sensors that could independently recover ego-motion or ego-velocity, such as wheel odometry and GPS devices. A rigorous multistage initialization approach is first developed to obtain reasonable initial guesses of spatiotemporal parameters without relying on prior knowledge of environmental information or specialized movements. Leveraging the IMU-centric principle, the spatiotemporal parameters of other sensors relative to IMU can be jointly optimized and refined via continuous-time batch estimation without sharing the overlapping field-of-views (FoVs) among exteroceptive sensors. A comprehensive series of experiments is carried out to quantitatively evaluate the proposed method in both simulation and real-world scenarios. The results demonstrate that the proposed method could achieve comparable calibration accuracy against state-of-the-art target-based calibration methods and outperform targetless calibration methods in terms of consistency and repeatability. © 2025 Elsevier B.V.

Improved Multi-Sensor Fusion Dynamic Odometry Based on Neural Networks
(2024) Sensors, 24 (19), art. no. 6193, Cited 9 times.
DOI: 10.3390/s24196193
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/85206439820?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Xi’an Institute of Applied Optics, Xi’an, 710065, China
ABSTRACT: High-precision simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) in dynamic real-world environments plays a crucial role in autonomous robot navigation, self-driving cars, and drone control. To address this dynamic localization issue, in this paper, a dynamic odometry method is proposed based on FAST-LIVO, a fast LiDAR (light detection and ranging)–inertial–visual odometry system, integrating neural networks with laser, camera, and inertial measurement unit modalities. The method first constructs visual–inertial and LiDAR–inertial odometry subsystems. Then, a lightweight neural network is used to remove dynamic elements from the visual part, and dynamic clustering is applied to the LiDAR part to eliminate dynamic environments, ensuring the reliability of the remaining environmental data. Validation of the datasets shows that the proposed multi-sensor fusion dynamic odometry can achieve high-precision pose estimation in complex dynamic environments with high continuity, reliability, and dynamic robustness. © 2024 by the authors.

AUTHOR FULL NAMES: Irfan, Mahammad (57220039222); Dalai, Sagar (57220023661); Trslic, Petar (57203132920); Riordan, James (8432943300); Dooly, Gerard (14123121400)

LSAF-LSTM-Based Self-Adaptive Multi-Sensor Fusion for Robust UAV State Estimation in Challenging Environments †
(2025) Machines, 13 (2), art. no. 130, Cited 15 times.
DOI: 10.3390/machines13020130
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/85219059669?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: CRIS Research Group, Department of Electronic and Computer Engineering, University of Limerick, V94 T9PX, Limerick, Ireland; School of Engineering, University of Limerick, The Lonsdale Building, Limerick, V94 T9PX, Ireland; Drone Systems Lab, School of Computing Engineering and Physical Science, University of the West of Scotland, Glasgow, G72 0LH, United Kingdom
ABSTRACT: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) state estimation is fundamental across applications like robot navigation, autonomous driving, virtual reality (VR), and augmented reality (AR). This research highlights the critical role of robust state estimation in ensuring safe and efficient autonomous UAV navigation, particularly in challenging environments. We propose a deep learning-based adaptive sensor fusion framework for UAV state estimation, integrating multi-sensor data from stereo cameras, an IMU, two 3D LiDAR’s, and GPS. The framework dynamically adjusts fusion weights in real time using a long short-term memory (LSTM) model, enhancing robustness under diverse conditions such as illumination changes, structureless environments, degraded GPS signals, or complete signal loss where traditional single-sensor SLAM methods often fail. Validated on an in-house integrated UAV platform and evaluated against high-precision RTK ground truth, the algorithm incorporates deep learning-predicted fusion weights into an optimization-based odometry pipeline. The system delivers robust, consistent, and accurate state estimation, outperforming state-of-the-art techniques. Experimental results demonstrate its adaptability and effectiveness across challenging scenarios, showcasing significant advancements in UAV autonomy and reliability through the synergistic integration of deep learning and sensor fusion. © 2025 by the authors.

Dynamic Evasion Point System for Mobile Robots
(2026) International Journal of Robotics and Control Systems, 6 (1), pp. 324 - 341, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.31763/ijrcs.v6i1.2232
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105034524877?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Information Technologies and Systems Research Center, Universidad Autónoma del Estado de Hidalgo, Carr. Tulancingo-Pachuca Km. 4.5, HGO., Pachuca de Soto, 42184, Mexico; LANAVEX, Universidad Politécnica de Pachuca, Carr. Pachuca-Cd. Sahagún Km. 20, Rancho Luna, Ex-Hacienda de Sta. Bárbara, HGO., Zempoala, 43830, Mexico
ABSTRACT: In this paper, a novel local path planner based on a complete Obstacle Avoidance Algorithm (OAA) and a Proportional-Derivative (PD) controller is developed for Mobile Robots (MR). The main contribution of this work is a local planner that generates global evasion points instead of just angles, and uses a normalized cost function that weights between the total Euclidean route distance and the orientation turning cost, separating the evasion algorithm from the pose tracking controller. ”Individual obstacles detected by the LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging sensor) are classified by measuring the distance between their corners. The OAA determines whether the mobile robot can drive through them or considers them as a single obstacle. A target point (an evasion point or the final goal) is selected by minimizing a normalized cost function. Various real experiments were carried out comparing the VPH and our method to illustrate the advantages and efficiency in both scenarios, achieving successful evasion in complex environments, such as ’U’ structures, and maintaining stable CPU usage. Our method uses a PD controller to drive both wheels and allows the mobile robot to reach its destination point in a smooth and efficient manner. © 2025 The Authors.

A Comprehensive Review of Sensing, Control, and Networking in Agricultural Robots: From Perception to Coordination
(2025) Robotics, 14 (11), art. no. 159, Cited 12 times.
DOI: 10.3390/robotics14110159
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105023128698?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Department of Biosystems and Agricultural Engineering, Oklahoma State University, Stillwater, 74078, OK, United States; Department of Biological Systems Engineering, Virginia Tech, Blacksburg, 24061, VA, United States; Department of Agricultural and Biological Engineering, Purdue University, West Lafayette, 47907, IN, United States; Department of Industrial & Enterprise Systems Engineering, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Champaign, 61801, IL, United States; Department of Computer Science, Oklahoma State University, Stillwater, 74078, OK, United States; Department of Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering, South Dakota State University, Brookings, 57007, SD, United States
ABSTRACT: This review critically examines advancements in sensing, control, and networking technologies for agricultural robots (AgRobots) and their impact on modern farming. AgRobots—including Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs), Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs), and robotic arms—are increasingly adopted to address labour shortages, sustainability challenges, and rising food demand. This paper reviews sensing technologies such as cameras, LiDAR, and multispectral sensors for navigation, object detection, and environmental perception. Control approaches, from classical PID (Proportional-Integral-Derivative) to advanced nonlinear and learning-based methods, are analysed to ensure precision, adaptability, and stability in dynamic agricultural settings. Networking solutions, including ZigBee, LoRaWAN, 5G, and emerging 6G, are evaluated for enabling real-time communication, multi-robot coordination, and data management. Swarm robotics and hybrid decentralized architectures are highlighted for efficient collective operations. This review is based on the literature published between 2015 and 2025 to identify key trends, challenges, and future directions in AgRobots. While AgRobots promise enhanced productivity, reduced environmental impact, and sustainable practices, barriers such as high costs, complex field conditions, and regulatory limitations remain. This review is expected to provide a foundation for guiding research and development toward innovative, integrated solutions for global food security and sustainable agriculture. © 2025 by the authors.
AUTHOR KEYWORDS: agricultural robots; control systems; networking strategies; precision agriculture; sensing technologies; sustainable farming practices; swarm robotics

LIO-LOT: Tightly-Coupled Multi-Object Tracking and LiDAR-Inertial Odometry
(2025) IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems, 26 (1), pp. 742 - 756, Cited 6 times.
DOI: 10.1109/TITS.2024.3488288
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/85208736497?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Wuhan University, School of Geodesy and Geomatics, Wuhan, 430079, China
ABSTRACT: Most existing LiDAR-Inertial odometry (LIO) systems heavily depend on the assumption of a static environment, which hinders their ability to effectively utilize dynamic objects in enhancing localization. Furthermore, accurate tracking of surrounding objects is crucial for emerging applications, such as autonomous driving and multi-robot collaboration. To this end, we present LIO-LOT, a tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial and multi-object tracking (MOT) system. In our system, each movable object is represented by a 3-D bounding box, derived from an object detector. Subsequently, these objects are associated with historical trajectories through a hybrid information matching strategy that integrates detections and geometric feature information. Considering tracking continuity and motion consistency, the associated objects are further categorized into high-confidence ones and low-confidence ones. Building upon this foundation, these two categories of objects are flexibly coupled with inertial measurement unit (IMU) pre-integration measurements and static scene structures to optimize the poses of both tracked objects and ego-vehicle under a factor graph optimization framework. For implementation, the aggregated information of high- and low-confidence objects are fully leveraged to form the object-related factors, which are hierarchically optimized with LIO, enhancing system stability in cases of poor object detections. The system's performance is extensively evaluated using the KITTI and nuScenes datasets. Experimental results explicitly demonstrate that the proposed system outperforms other state-of-the-art methods in terms of ego-localization and multi-object tracking, particularly in highly dynamic scenarios with situations of occlusion and truncation. © 2024 IEEE.

BIM-based Adaptive Monte Carlo Localization (AMCL) method for indoor mobile robot
(2026) Measurement: Journal of the International Measurement Confederation, 271, art. no. 120943, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.1016/j.measurement.2026.120943
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105031224825?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: School of Transportation, Shijiazhuang Tiedao University, Shijiazhuang, 050043, China; POWERCHINA Chengdu Engineering Corporation Limited, Chengdu, 611130, China; School of Civil and Construction Engineering, Oregon State University, Corvallis, 97331, OR, United States; Hebei Key Laboratory of Traffic Safety and Control, Shijiazhuang, 050043, China
ABSTRACT: This paper presents an enhanced BIM-based Adaptive Monte Carlo Localization (AMCL) algorithm designed to overcome two critical technical barriers facing indoor mobile robotics: (1) the difficulty in acquiring a mobile robot's priori information, and (2) insufficient localization accuracy in indoor environment. The study analyzes and extracts geometric and semantic information of interior space structure through a Building Information Model (BIM), then building multi-layer raster maps for localization and navigation applications. The semantic layer map serves as a priori information to fuse a mobile robot's LiDAR and vision sensor measurement information during the mobile robot operation. The proposed BIM-AMCL method improves obtaining prior information required for localization from BIM and optimizes the localization process. The experimental results demonstrate that the BIM-AMCL method maintains errors within 10 cm for both global and tracking localization processes, and within 5° for orientation error. Compared to the lidar-only AMCL approach, the proposed method achieves a 41.69% reduction in positional error and a 60.71% decrease in angular error, with a 55.56% improvement in global localization speed. Furthermore, by leveraging BIM-derived prior knowledge, the robot attains immediate localization and navigation capabilities without requiring environmental exploration. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

MDU-sampling: Multi-domain uniform sampling method for large-scale outdoor LiDAR point cloud registration
(2024) Electronics Letters, 60 (5), art. no. e13129, Cited 4 times.
DOI: 10.1049/ell2.13129
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/85186558605?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: College of Physics and Information Engineering, Fuzhou University, Fuzhou, China
ABSTRACT: Sampling is a crucial concern for outdoor light detection and ranging (LiDAR) point cloud registration due to the large amounts of point cloud. Numerous algorithms have been devised to tackle this issue by selecting key points. However, these approaches often necessitate extensive computations, giving rise to challenges related to computational time and complexity. This letter proposes a multi-domain uniform sampling method (MDU-sampling) for large-scale outdoor LiDAR point cloud registration. The feature extraction based on deep learning aggregates information from the neighbourhood, so there is redundancy between adjacent features. The sampling method in this paper is carried out in the spatial and feature domains. First, uniform sampling is executed in the spatial domain, maintaining local point cloud uniformity. This is believed to preserve more potential point correspondences and is beneficial for subsequent neighbourhood information aggregation and feature sampling. Subsequently, a secondary sampling in the feature domain is performed to reduce redundancy among the features of neighbouring points. Notably, only points on the same ring in LiDAR data are considered as neighbouring points, eliminating the need for additional neighbouring point search and thereby speeding up processing rates. Experimental results demonstrate that the approach enhances accuracy and robustness compared with benchmarks. © 2024 The Authors. Electronics Letters published by John Wiley & Sons Ltd on behalf of The Institution of Engineering and Technology.

FLARE-SLAM: Multibeam Feature Extraction and Residual Enhancement for 3-D LiDAR Mapping
(2025) IEEE Internet of Things Journal, 12 (14), pp. 26620 - 26632, Cited 2 times.
DOI: 10.1109/JIOT.2025.3563186
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105003667330?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Institute of Intelligent Instruments and Measurement Controlling Technology, Jilin University, Key Laboratory of Geophysical Exploration Equipment, College of Instrumentation and Electrical Engineering, Jilin, Changchun, 130061, China
ABSTRACT: This article introduces a novel multisensor fusion simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) algorithm named FLARE-SLAM, designed for mobile robots operating in complex environments. This algorithm addresses challenges associated with uneven light detection and ranging (LiDAR) measurement signals and their random distribution. First, we enhance the stability of feature extraction by refining the curvature calculation strategy for LiDAR point clouds and incorporating contextual information from the sensor array. Second, we introduce an adaptive residual optimization weight distribution mechanism, grounded in the principle of uniform residual optimization, to boost the algorithm’s adaptability across various environments. Extensive evaluations on the KITTI dataset confirm that FLARE-SLAM constructs a global map with enhanced consistency and accuracy, achieving an absolute trajectory error of 0.53% and an absolute rotation error of 0.19°/100 m. Additionally, we validate the robustness of the algorithm through real-world testing in diverse outdoor and indoor settings. © 2014 IEEE.

Li X., Du B.
AUTHOR FULL NAMES: Li, Xiuzhi (23028270800); Du, Bowen (59556828000)
23028270800; 59556828000
RL-LVIS: a robust, lightweight LiDAR–visual–inertial state estimator and mapping for mobile robots
(2025) Advanced Robotics, 39 (8), pp. 424 - 440, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.1080/01691864.2025.2497414
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105004307468?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: School of Information Science and Technology, Beijing University of Technology, Beijing, China; Beijing Key Laboratory of Computational Intelligence and Intelligent System, Beijing, China
ABSTRACT: In recent years, the application of autonomous outdoor robots has faced challenges in improving the computational efficiency and robustness of underlying algorithms due to the limitations of size and weight, making it difficult to use high-quality sensors and powerful processors. This paper introduces a robust, lightweight, and high-precision framework tailored for outdoor mobile robots to achieve robust and accurate state estimation. We unify LiDAR, visual, and inertial measurements within the framework of Iterated-Error-State Kalman Filter (IESKF), by constructing multi-state-constrained visual observations and calculating visual reprojection errors, rather than using computationally expensive graph optimization methods. In order to reduce the computational load of the system, we maintain the Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) states within a sliding window by state cloning and updating the finite-sized state dimension. Due to its simplicity, we derived the formulas for the proposed framework on differential manifolds. Leveraging data from these three sensors, our system maintains comparable accuracy to optimization algorithms in three large-scale scenes while ensuring normal operation in scenarios where visual or LiDAR measurements degrade. Our experiments validate that the proposed system has low computational load, making it suitable for operation on embedded platforms with limited computational resources. © 2025 Informa UK Limited, trading as Taylor & Francis Group and The Robotics Society of Japan.

Brenner M., Reyes N.H., Susnjak T., Barczak A.L.C.

RGB-D and Thermal Sensor Fusion: A Systematic Literature Review
(2023) IEEE Access, 11, pp. 82410 - 82442, Cited 77 times.
DOI: 10.1109/ACCESS.2023.3301119
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/85166780788?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Massey University, School of Mathematical and Computational Sciences, Auckland, 0632, New Zealand; Bond University, Centre for Data Analytics, Gold Coast, 4226 , QLD, Australia
ABSTRACT: In the last decade, the computer vision field has seen significant progress in multimodal data fusion and learning, where multiple sensors, including depth, infrared, and visual, are used to capture the environment across diverse spectral ranges. Despite these advancements, there has been no systematic and comprehensive evaluation of fusing RGB-D and thermal modalities to date. While autonomous driving using LiDAR, radar, RGB, and other sensors has garnered substantial research interest, along with the fusion of RGB and depth modalities, the integration of thermal cameras and, specifically, the fusion of RGB-D and thermal data, has received comparatively less attention. This might be partly due to the limited number of publicly available datasets for such applications. This paper provides a comprehensive review of both, state-of-the-art and traditional methods used in fusing RGB-D and thermal camera data for various applications, such as site inspection, human tracking, fault detection, and others. The reviewed literature has been categorised into technical areas, such as 3D reconstruction, segmentation, object detection, available datasets, and other related topics. Following a brief introduction and an overview of the methodology, the study delves into calibration and registration techniques, then examines thermal visualisation and 3D reconstruction, before discussing the application of classic feature-based techniques and modern deep learning approaches. The paper concludes with a discourse on current limitations and potential future research directions. It is hoped that this survey will serve as a valuable reference for researchers looking to familiarise themselves with the latest advancements and contribute to the RGB-DT research field.  © 2013 IEEE.

WeCo-SLAM: Wearable Cooperative SLAM System for Real-Time Indoor Localization under Challenging Conditions
(2022) IEEE Sensors Journal, 22 (6), pp. 5122 - 5132, Cited 32 times.
DOI: 10.1109/JSEN.2021.3101121
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/85111599769?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Ibisc, Université d'Évry, Université Paris-Saclay, Évry-Courcouronnes, 91020, France; Innodura Tb, Villeurbanne, 69603, France; Titane Project-Team, Inria Sophia Antipolis-Méditerrannée Research Centre, Valbonne, 06902, France
ABSTRACT: Real-Time globally consistent GPS tracking is critical for an accurate localization and is crucial for applications such as autonomous navigation or multi-robot mapping. However, under challenging environment conditions such as indoor/outdoor transitions, GPS signals are partially available or not consistent over time. In this paper, a real-Time tracking system for continuously locating emergency response agents in challenging conditions is presented. A cooperative localization method based on Laser-Visual-Inertial (LVI) and GPS sensors is achieved by communicating optimization events between a LiDAR-Inertial-SLAM (LI-SLAM) and Visual-Inertial-SLAM (VI-SLAM) that operate simultaneously. The estimation of the pose assisted by multiple SLAM approaches provides the GPS localization of the agent when a stand-Alone GPS fails. The system has been tested under the terms of the MALIN Challenge, which aims to globally localize agents across outdoor and indoor environments under challenging conditions (such as smoked rooms, stairs, indoor/outdoor transitions, repetitive patterns, extreme lighting changes) where it is well known that a stand-Alone SLAM will not be enough to maintaining the localization. The system achieved Absolute Trajectory Error of 0.48%, with a pose update rate between 15 and 20 Hz. Furthermore, the system is able to build a global consistent 3D LiDAR Map that is post-processed to create a 3D reconstruction at different level of details. © 2001-2012 IEEE.

Liu E., Li H., Li S., Cheng X.
AUTHOR FULL NAMES: Liu, Ensong (58967394800); Li, Haozhen (58967627200); Li, Sijiang (57945092200); Cheng, Xiang (55546390900)

Centralized Multi-Robot Collaborative LiDAR SLAM Utilizing Loop Closure Selection
(2023) Proceedings - 2023 China Automation Congress, CAC 2023, pp. 463 - 468, Cited 2 times.
DOI: 10.1109/CAC59555.2023.10450881
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/85189373149?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: School of Electronics, Peking University, Beijing, China
ABSTRACT: Multi-robot systems have attracted much attention due to their high efficiency and robustness. Multi-robot Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) is the cornerstone of collaboration, such that each robot can localize and build a map of the workspace. One of the key challenges of this problem lies in utilizing the shared information between robots adequately so that the system can retain the correct information and reject the outliers. Here we propose a centralized multi-robot collaborative LiDAR SLAM framework for robots, each only equipped with a 2D LiDAR without the need for additional sensors. With each robot able to run simple LiDAR odometry onboard, a central server with greater computational capacity collects the information from robots, optimizes their poses globally, and updates their poses through communication. For a large number of loop closures in multi-robot SLAM systems, it is catastrophic to build wrong data associations between pose nodes in the global factor graph. We resort to a loop closure selection method to ensure the correctness and consistency of global optimization. Throughout the verification process on the real Automated Mobile Robot (AMR) platform, the framework exhibits better performance on localization and mapping.  © 2023 IEEE.

Swarm-SLAM: Sparse Decentralized Collaborative Simultaneous Localization and Mapping Framework for Multi-Robot Systems
(2024) IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters, 9 (1), pp. 475 - 482, Cited 137 times.
DOI: 10.1109/LRA.2023.3333742
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/85178017203?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Polytechnique Montréal, Department of Computer and Software Engineering, Montreal, H3T 1J4, QC, Canada
ABSTRACT: Collaborative Simultaneous Localization And Mapping (C-SLAM) is a vital component for successful multi-robot operations in environments without an external positioning system, such as indoors, underground or underwater. In this paper, we introduce Swarm-SLAM, an open-source C-SLAM system that is designed to be scalable, flexible, decentralized, and sparse, which are all key properties in swarm robotics. Our system supports lidar, stereo, and RGB-D sensing, and it includes a novel inter-robot loop closure prioritization technique that reduces communication and accelerates convergence. We evaluated our ROS 2 implementation on five different datasets, and in a real-world experiment with three robots communicating through an ad-hoc network.  © 2016 IEEE.

Chen B., Zhao H., Zhu R., Hu Y.
AUTHOR FULL NAMES: Chen, Baifan (25652713200); Zhao, Haowu (57222571410); Zhu, Ruyi (57754124400); Hu, Yemin (57753785300)
25652713200; 57222571410; 57754124400; 57753785300
Marked‐LIEO: Visual Marker‐Aided LiDAR/IMU/Encoder Integrated Odometry
(2022) Sensors, 22 (13), art. no. 4749, Cited 14 times.
DOI: 10.3390/s22134749
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/85132434257?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: School of Automation, Central South University, Changsha, 410017, China; School of Resources and Safety Engineering, Central South University, Changsha, 410017, China
ABSTRACT: In this paper, we propose a visual marker‐aided LiDAR/IMU/encoder integrated odometry, Marked‐LIEO, to achieve pose estimation of mobile robots in an indoor long corridor environment. In the first stage, we design the pre‐integration model of encoder and IMU respectively to realize the pose estimation combined with the pose estimation from the second stage providing prediction for the Li‐ DAR odometry. In the second stage, we design low‐frequency visual marker odometry, which is optimized jointly with LiDAR odometry to obtain the final pose estimation. In view of the wheel slipping and LiDAR degradation problems, we design an algorithm that can make the optimization weight of encoder odometry and LiDAR odometry adjust adaptively according to yaw angle and LiDAR degradation distance respectively. Finally, we realize the multi‐sensor fusion localization through joint optimization of an encoder, IMU, LiDAR, and camera measurement information. Aiming at the problems of GNSS information loss and LiDAR degradation in indoor corridor environment, this method introduces the state prediction information of encoder and IMU and the absolute observation information of visual marker to achieve the accurate pose of indoor corridor environment, which has been verified by experiments in Gazebo simulation environment and real environment. © 2022 by the authors. Licensee MDPI, Basel, Switzerland.

Qi G., Ma D., Du Y., Cao X., Chen H.
AUTHOR FULL NAMES: Qi, Guoqing (57921361200); Ma, Daoyi (58247583900); Du, Yunben (57921168100); Cao, Xiangxiang (57921428600); Chen, Hao (58248005100)

Research on SLAM of Mobile Robot Based on Fusion of Laser and Vision
(2023) Proceedings of SPIE - The International Society for Optical Engineering, 12594, art. no. 125940V, Cited 1 times.
DOI: 10.1117/12.2671329
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/85159188466?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Ocean College, Jiangsu University of Science and Technology, Zhenjiang, 212000, China
ABSTRACT: In the complex environment simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) system, the use of a single laser or visual sensor is susceptible to external factors, which affects the accuracy of mobile robot mapping. A SLAM mapping method based on vision, LIDAR and encoder fusion is designed. Firstly, LIDAR and encoder data are fused by extended Kalman filter (EKF) method. Then, the data obtained by the depth camera is converted into the virtual two-dimensional laser radar data. Through the adaptive weighted fusion algorithm, the EKF fusion results are weighted fusion with the camera processing data, and the fused data is used to construct the map. The experimental results of the actual environment show that the method of multi-sensor data fusion is better than single sensor in the accuracy of mapping, and can establish a map closer to the actual environment. © 2023 SPIE.

Xu K., Zhang B., Li J., Wang G., Sun M.
AUTHOR FULL NAMES: Xu, Kun (60022589400); Zhang, Boheng (57199727115); Li, Jiangang (58640942700); Wang, Guizhong (57201076966); Sun, Mingjian (42162312100)

UKF-Based Multi-sensor Data Processing Algorithm for SLAM
(2023) 2023 9th International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering, ICCSSE 2023, pp. 361 - 368, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.1109/ICCSSE59359.2023.10245624
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/85173901742?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: School of Information Science and Engineering, Harbin Institute of Technology, Weihai, China; Harbin Institute of Technology, Department of Control Science and Engineering, Harbin, China; Woan Technology (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd., Shenzhen, China; Hebei Key Laboratory of Grid Advanced Measurement, Monitor Jinyanhagong Industrial Technology Research Institute, Zhangjiakou, China
ABSTRACT: Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) algorithm is widely used in unmanned and robotic applications. SLAM usually uses sensor data, which are from the LiDAR, the inertial measurement unit (IMU) and the wheeled odometry, to build maps of the surrounding environment. However, the motion distortion of LiDAR data and the error accumulation of wheeled odometry can affect the accuracy of the front-end odometry of the SLAM algorithm, which can lead to serious errors in the maps created. Therefore, in order to solve the problem of poor map construction results of SLAM algorithm due to various types of sensor errors. we propose the traceless Kalman filtering based (UKF-based) multi-sensor data processing algorithm. Firstly, the proposed algorithm uses the UKF to fuse IMU and wheeled odometry data to reduce the cumulative error of wheeled odometry. And then the algorithm uses IMU and corrected wheeled odometry data and combines with the motion states of the robot to solve the motion distortion problem of LiDAR data. Finally, we verified the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm for wheeled odometry data correction in Gazebo simulation environment and real environment experiments, and compared the mapping effectiveness of SLAM by using the original data and the data processed by our algorithm. The experimental results show that the map construction effect of SLAM algorithm is significantly improved when using the sensor data processed by the algorithm. Experimental validation on the robot shows that the proposed algorithm has universal applicability and good compatibility.  © 2023 IEEE.

Wang J., Zuo X., Zhao X., Lyu J., Liu Y.
AUTHOR FULL NAMES: Wang, Jinke (57468035600); Zuo, Xingxing (57200629420); Zhao, Xiangrui (57215561026); Lyu, Jiajun (57468501500); Liu, Yong (56011543900)
57468035600; 57200629420; 57215561026; 57468501500; 56011543900
Review of multi-source fusion SLAM: current status and challenges [多源融合SLAM的现状与挑战]
(2022) Journal of Image and Graphics, 27 (2), pp. 368 - 389, Cited 33 times.
DOI: 10.11834/jig.210547
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/85125351663?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, 310027, China
ABSTRACT: Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) technology is widely used in mobile robot applications, and it focuses on the robot's motion state estimation issue and reconstructing the environment model (map) at the same time. The SLAM science community has promoted the technique to be deployed in various applications in real life nowadays, such as virtual reality, augmented reality, autonomous driving, service robots, etc. In complicated scenarios, SLAM systems empowered with single sensor such as a camera or light detection and ranging(LiDAR) often fail to customize the targeted applications due to the deficiency of accuracy and robustness. Current research analyses have gradually improved SLAM solutions based on multi-sensors, multiple feature primitives, and the integration of multi-dimensional information. This research reviews current methods in the multi-source fusion SLAM realm at three scales: multi-sensor fusion (hybrid system with two or more kinds of sensors such as camera, LiDAR and inertial measurement unit (IMU), and combination methods can be divided into two categories(the loosely-coupled and the tightly-coupled), multi-feature-primitive fusion (point, line, plane, other high-dimensional geometric features, and the featureless direct-based method) and multi-dimensional information fusion (geometric information, semantic information, physical information, and inferred information from deep neural networks). The challenges and future research of multi-source fusion SLAM has been predicted as well. Multi-source fusion systems can implement accurate and robust state estimation and mapping, which can meet the requirements in a wider variety of applications. For instance, the fusion of vision and inertial sensors can illustrate the drift and scale missing issue of visual odometry, while the fusion of LiDAR and inertial measurement unit can improve the system's robustness, especially in unstructured or degraded scenes. The fusion of other sensors, such as sonar, radar and GPS(global positioning system) can extend the applicability further. In addition, the fusion of diverse geometric feature primitives such as feature points, lines, curves, planes, curved surfaces, cubes, and featureless direct-based methods can greatly deduct the degree of valid constraints, which is of great importance for state estimation systems. The reconstructed environmental map with multiple feature primitives is informative in autonomous navigation tasks. Furthermore, data-driven deep-learning-based synthesized analysis in the context of probabilistic model-based methods paves a new path to overcome the challenges of the initial SLAM systems. The learning-based methods (supervised learning, unsupervised learning, and hybrid supervised learning) are gradually applied to various modules of the SLAM system, including relative pose regression, map representation, loop closure detection, and unrolled back-end optimization, etc. Learning-based methods will benefit the performance of SLAM more with more cutting-edge research to fill the gap amongst networks and various original methods. This demonstration is shown as following: 1) The analysis of funder mental mechanisms of multi-sensor fusion and current multi-sensor fusion methods are illustrated; 2) Multi-feature primitive fusion and multi-dimensional information fusion are demonstrated; 3) The current difficulties and challenges of multi-source fusion towards SLAM have been issued; 4) The executive summary has been implemented at the end. © 2022, Editorial Office of Journal of Image and Graphics. All right reserved.
